title: Generative AI Availability, Grades, and Student Satisfaction at a Large University
abstract: arXiv:2607.21534v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The availability of generative AI (GenAI) has raised concerns that college students substitute GenAI for cognitive effort, earning high grades without learning. If this "GenAI substitution hypothesis" is true, grades should rise disproportionately in GenAI-susceptible courses--those relying more on assessments like take-home problem sets and essays rather than in-class exams. Student satisfaction (self-reported understanding and interest) may also shift. We test this hypothesis using syllabus and administrative data from a large U.S. university (2016-2025; 138,386 students; 72,730 course offerings). We measure GenAI susceptibility by extracting assessment types from syllabi with a human-validated LLM pipeline. We then use a difference-in-differences design comparing courses before and after ChatGPT's release, modeling COVID-19 effects as persistent or transient. Effects on grades and satisfaction are small and sensitive to COVI

translated_title: 一所大型大学中生成式AI的可用性、成绩与学生满意度
translated_abstract: 生成式人工智能（GenAI）的普及引发了一种担忧：大学生可能会用生成式AI替代自身的认知努力，在没有真正学习的情况下获得高分。如果这一“生成式AI替代假说”成立，那么在易受生成式AI影响的课程中——即那些更多依赖课后问题集和论文等评估方式而非课堂考试的课程——成绩应当出现不成比例的上涨。学生的满意度（自我报告的理解程度和兴趣）也可能随之改变。我们利用美国一所大型大学的教学大纲与行政数据（2016-2025年；138,386名学生；72,730门课程开设记录）检验了这一假说。我们通过一个经过人工验证的大语言模型流程，从教学大纲中提取评估类型，以此衡量各课程对生成式AI的易感程度。随后采用双重差分设计，比较ChatGPT发布前后的课程差异，并将新冠疫情的影响建模为持续性或暂时性效应。研究结果显示，生成式AI对成绩和满意度的影响很小，且对新冠疫情的建模方式较为敏感。
tldr: 该研究利用一所美国大型大学2016-2025年、涵盖13.8万余名学生的数据，通过双重差分方法发现ChatGPT发布后易受生成式AI影响的课程在成绩和学生满意度上变化很小，“生成式AI替代学习导致高分”的担忧未得到有力支持。
en_tdlr: Using difference-in-differences analysis of administrative data covering 138,386 students at a large U.S. university from 2016-2025, this study finds that grades and student satisfaction changed only slightly in GenAI-susceptible courses after ChatGPT's release, providing little support for the "GenAI substitution hypothesis."
